doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Playing the world with Basie and recommending musicians
summary: The band was one of Basie's best; Wess recommended many players such as Eddie Jones, Thad Jones, Sonny Cohn and Al Aarons.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: What was it like playing in different parts of the world with the Basie band?

Oh, we always had a good following. And the band was hot. We were in one of the best bands Basie ever had. And that’s the band that made him rich, you know. The band was tight. I had forgotten actually, how good the band was until I was listening to those Mosaic recordings. And then it came back to me, how good that band was. It was like one person playing, you know. Everybody was—it was a good band. Well Basie, he knew how to do that. You know he didn’t fault nobody. He just let it stay there until the cats got it together, and then when they got it together he knew what to do with it. But you know the fellows in the band did all of that. He didn’t know too many people, really, I mean musicians. When he’d want somebody, you know he’d say, “hey Magic, I need a trumpet player—I need a trombone player—I need a bass”—I need this—I need that. And I’d tell him who to call. I got Eddie Jones in the band, Bill Hughes, Sonny Cohn, Eric Dixon, Thad Jones, I can’t think, oh Al Aarons. Yeah I got a whole lot of people in the band, you know. And when I left I recommended Danny Turner but he didn’t know Danny so he didn’t know that Danny could play lead, so he got Bobby Plater. He knew Bobby Plater could play lead. But I recommended Danny Turner to him when I left.
